title: Konosuke Matsushita's 250-Year Mission
text:
Konosuke Matsushita founded his electrical goods company in Osaka in 1918, making plug sockets with his wife and brother-in-law. By the early 1930s it was a growing business, but he was searching for a deeper reason for it to exist.

On May 5, 1932, he gathered his employees and announced what he called the company's true mission. A manufacturer's purpose, he said, was to overcome poverty by producing goods as abundant and cheap as tap water, which people take freely from the street without anyone objecting. The company would pursue that goal over 250 years, divided into ten periods of twenty-five years each. The current generation would work through the first period, and their successors would carry the work forward.

Matsushita later wrote that the employees responded with great excitement, and that many came forward to speak about their commitment. The company counted 1932 as the first year of its founding mission.

The firm, later known as Panasonic, became one of the largest electronics makers in the world. Matsushita's "tap water philosophy" and the idea of a mission beyond profit became central to how Japanese management was discussed.
lesson: People work harder for a purpose that outlasts them than for a profit target. Give them a reason that is worth handing on.
source: Panasonic corporate history; Konosuke Matsushita, Quest for Prosperity (1988)
